spec_match.rationale: The markup is the genuine declarative pattern: interestfor on menubar buttons and submenu items targeting popover=hint panels — exactly the surface the feature ships.

interactive.rationale: Interactivity is fully delegated to the engine (hover/focus interest opens panels) with zero page script — legitimate where interestfor exists, but on engines without it (measured here) nothing on the page is operable and there is no probe, readout, or fallback interaction.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Promises 'hover, keyboard, or touch — the cascade behaves like every desktop menu'; on non-supporting engines nothing behaves at all.

edge_cases.rationale: The info banner claims 'Without it the menus still open but the layout falls back to default top-left' — measured FALSE on Chromium 141: interestForElement is absent from HTMLButtonElement.prototype, so hover produces nothing and the menus never open (hint popovers themselves parse fine: showPopover on popover=hint works). Misleading-fallback copy is a named anti-regression class.

references.rationale: Feature index links the chromestatus entry; this page itself links only siblings.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite exists; this page adds no probe anchoring its own claims.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP run: 'interestForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype = false; attributes present in DOM; popover=hint parses and opens programmatically; 0px overflow both classes; zero console errors. The cascade itself could not be exercised because the engine lacks the invoker — precisely the state the page fails to disclose.

telemetry_health.rationale: No telemetry assert on the page.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables; amber-bordered info block on stone reads fine.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons throughout (good); but with the invoker absent the menu buttons are focusable controls that do nothing, with no state exposed — and no aria-expanded equivalents are rendered by the page for unsupported engines.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000 (measured); hover-driven interest needs the touch/keyboard paths the feature itself defines, which the page correctly defers to the engine.

openQuestions.title: Replace the false fallback claim with a live support probe
openQuestions.detail: Measured on Chromium 141: the banner's 'menus still open' claim is wrong — without interestForElement nothing opens. Probe 'interestForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype, state support honestly with the real flag steps, and on unsupported engines give the panels a click-to-open fallback (popovertarget) so the cascade remains explorable.

openQuestions.title: Add a telemetry assert and interest-state readout
openQuestions.detail: A small script reporting which panel currently has interest (via toggle events) would give the page a live readout and health signal.

guidanceConsulted.query: interest invokers hover focus popover hint
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use interestfor/hint for hover-interest surfaces with graceful degradation.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Pattern used correctly for supporting engines; degradation is the filed gap.

summary: Reviewed headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the declarative markup is right, but the page's fallback claim is measurably false on non-supporting engines (nothing opens; probed: interestForElement absent while hint popovers parse) — filed as the major fix, with a click-fallback proposal that keeps the cascade explorable everywhere.
